meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the E-101 unit
meta.scope: From TK-101 and the BFW pumps P-101A/B through E-101 to the BFW delivery to the boiler house, and from the flash-steam header (PI-105) through XV-100 and FV-104 to the shell with its vent V-104, vacuum breaker VB-101 and PSV-100, and the condensate trap set to the return header; the SIS (XV-100 trips) and the utilities (instrument air, electrical power). Excluded: the upstream flash-steam plant, the condensate return beyond the header and the boiler house (recorded as causes and consequences at the interfaces).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
Running pump P-101A trips (motor, power)
P-101B unavailable (motor fault) or not started
TK-101 empty
suction valve closed
N1.cons: No BFW to the boiler house: boiler low drum level, boiler trip or dry firing (outside the unit). Steam on stagnant water in the E-101 tubes: local boiling and hammer. Shell drawn to vacuum once the steam is cut

N1.causes:
Pump wear or cavitation
low TK-101 level
partly closed suction valve
N1.cons: BFW short at the boiler house; hotter outlet at the same steam; pump damage

N1.causes:
Make-up to TK-101 stopped
tank drain left open
N1.cons: Pump cavitation, then no flow (see N1 Flow NO)

N1.causes:
Make-up more than consumption
recycle high at low demand
N1.cons: Overflow of treated water with chemicals to drain

N1.causes: Valve closed downstream of E-101 or at the boiler house while FIC-101 drives FV-101A open and FV-101B shut
N1.cons: Pump at shut-off (1030 kPa g) with no flow: water overheats, seal fails, hot-water spray

N1.causes:
Low TK-101 level
hot BFW in TK-101
plugged suction
N1.cons: Cavitation, noise, flow loss, pump damage

N1.dev: Reverse flow through the idle pump
N1.causes: Passing check valve on the idle pump
N1.cons: Recirculation through the idle pump, less forward flow, idle pump spins backwards

N1.causes:
Hot make-up or condensate routed to the tank
BFW inlet up to 15 °C hotter
N1.cons: Less NPSH; outlet control keeps 70 °C with less steam
More steam needed (14.6 % more in the model, shell 153 kPa g): FV-104 loses its margin; outlet may fall below target

N1.dev: Oxygen, hardness or wrong treatment chemical in the BFW
N1.cons: Corrosion or scale in the tubes (tube leak later), boiler deposits; exposure when sampling

N1.causes:
Spare started against a closed discharge
running pump stopped first
N1.cons: BFW interrupted: FSLL-101 closes XV-100; boiler house loses BFW

sg.text: FSLL-101 trip closes XV-100 (< 30 m³/h, 5 s) (model: trip at 7.5 s)
Operator rounds only (no level instrument on the P&ID)
FV-101B complementary recycle (protects only against FV-101A closing)
FSLL-101 trip closes XV-100 (< 30 m³/h, 5 s)

recs.text: Auto-start P-101B on a P-101A trip or low discharge pressure (PI-106 transmitter, recommended addition), completing inside the FSLL-101 delay; test the spare start monthly.
Add level transmitter LT-101 (recommended addition) on TK-101 with a low-level alarm and a low-low pump trip, and a high-level alarm for overfill.
Provide a fixed minimum-flow line with restriction orifice from the pump discharge to TK-101, independent of FV-101B, so a blocked outlet downstream of E-101 cannot deadhead the running pump.
Confirm a check valve on each pump discharge and on the BFW line to the boiler house; add them to the inspection plan.
Agree the interface with the boiler house: shared alarms for FIC-101 LO and TIAH-108 HI, a call-out procedure, and include loss of BFW and hot BFW from E-101 in the boiler-house HAZOP.
Water-treatment control: BFW hardness and oxygen-scavenger sampling programme; closed sampling point and PPE for treatment chemicals.
